ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, $\angle B = \angle D = 90^\circ$, $BC = CD$, $\angle 1 = 40^\circ$, then what is the value of $\angle 2$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given $\because$ $\angle B = \angle D = 90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ $\triangle ABC$ and $\triangle ADC$ are both right-angled triangles,\\
In $\triangle ABC$ and $\triangle ADC$,\\
$\left\{\begin{array}{c} BC = DC \\ AC = AC \end{array}\right.$,\\
$\therefore$ $\triangle ABC \cong \triangle ADC$ (HL),\\
$\therefore$ $\angle 1 = \angle CAD = 40^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle 2 = 90^\circ - \angle CAD = \boxed{50^\circ}$.
